title: Inhibition of STING signaling by H-151 attenuates acute lung injury and systemic inflammatory response in murine cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Li, W., Zhang, K., Liu, X., et al.
abstract:
Background: STING activation contributes to hyperinflammatory cytokine storms. We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of small-molecule STING inhibitor H-151 in murine polymicrobial sepsis.
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to CLP. Mice received intraperitoneal H-151 (10 mg/kg) or vehicle 1 hour post-surgery. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), lung histology, cytokine levels, and 7-day survival were recorded.
Results: H-151 treatment significantly suppressed lung neutrophil infiltration, reduced circulating TNF-α and IL-6, and boosted 7-day survival from 30% to 65% (p = 0.014).
Conclusion: Pharmacological inhibition of STING represents a viable therapeutic strategy in polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CLP model, therapeutic intervention H-151 administered post-CLP, reports survival and lung injury, published 2022.
learning_pearl: Classic CLP paper evaluating a small molecule inhibitor post-surgery. Clear INCLUDE.

title: Curcumin alleviates lipopolysaccharide-induced myocardial dysfunction and pyroptosis through NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition in mice
authors: Yang, H., Chen, G., Wang, Y.
abstract:
Background: Septic cardiomyopathy involves cardiac pyroptosis and contractile failure. Here, we examined curcumin's protective effect against LPS cardiotoxicity.
Methods: C57BL/6 mice were challenged with intraperitoneal LPS (15 mg/kg) to induce septic shock. Curcumin (100 mg/kg) was gavaged 2 hours prior to LPS injection. Echocardiography, cardiac caspase-1 activity, and serum troponin T were assessed.
Results: Curcumin significantly preserved ejection fraction, blunted serum troponin elevation, and diminished cardiomyocyte cleavage of gasdermin D.
Conclusion: Curcumin prevents LPS-induced septic cardiac dysfunction by inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent pyroptosis.
rationale: Model violation: Challenge was pure intraperitoneal Lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Pure LPS challenge models are strictly excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Always verify the induction method: pure LPS injection is an automatic EXCLUDE under EX-LPS!

title: Colon ascendants stent peritonitis (CASP) model in rats: Therapeutic impact of delayed peritoneal irrigation with ozonated saline
authors: Kovacs, T., Nemeth, N., Peto, K., et al.
abstract:
Aims: Colon ascendants stent peritonitis (CASP) creates continuous fecal leakage simulating ruptured appendicitis or surgical anastomotic dehiscence. We tested whether delayed peritoneal irrigation with ozonated saline improves outcomes.
Materials and Methods: Wistar rats underwent CASP surgery via surgical implantation of an 18G stent into the ascending colon. Six hours post-surgery, relaparotomy and peritoneal lavage using ozonated saline (10 μg/mL) or normal saline were conducted. Microcirculation, bacteremia, and 5-day survival were tracked.
Key Findings: Ozonated lavage decreased systemic bacteremia by 85%, preserved mesenteric capillary perfusion, and significantly improved 5-day survival (60% vs 20%, p = 0.008).
Significance: Adjunctive peritoneal washing with ozonated saline mitigates polymicrobial peritoneal sepsis in CASP rats.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved CASP model (continuous fecal leakage), therapeutic lavage intervention, 2020 publication date.
learning_pearl: CASP (Colon Ascendants Stent Peritonitis) is explicitly listed as an approved model in our protocol!

title: Melatonin inhibits gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis in cultured bone marrow-derived macrophages during septic stimulation
authors: Deng, Z., Song, L., Wu, T.
abstract:
Background: Pyroptotic macrophage lysis fuels systemic inflammatory cascades. We explored melatonin's cytoprotective mechanisms in primary macrophages.
Methods: Mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were harvested from healthy mice and stimulated ex vivo with heat-inactivated Escherichia coli O111:B4 in the presence of melatonin (1-50 μM). LDH release, IL-1β secretion, and ASC speck formation were measured.
Results: Melatonin markedly reduced LDH release and suppressed caspase-1 cleavage in cultured BMDMs without affecting cellular viability.
Conclusion: Melatonin prevents macrophage pyroptotic cell death in vitro, offering molecular insights for sepsis therapy.
rationale: Model violation: Ex vivo cultured primary cells (BMDMs) in petri dishes. No live animals received sepsis or treatment.
learning_pearl: Cultured primary cells (e.g., BMDMs) tested ex vivo in culture dishes are EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Maternal probiotic supplementation prevents necrotizing enterocolitis and systemic neonatal sepsis in newborn rat pups
authors: Hansen, M. E., Berg, A. K., Poulsen, T. M., et al.
abstract:
Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) frequently escalates into fatal neonatal sepsis. We investigated maternal dietary probiotic administration on pup intestinal barrier defense.
Methods: Pregnant Sprague-Dawley dams received Bifidobacterium infantis or control chow. Newborn pups were subjected to an experimental NEC protocol comprising formula feeding, hypoxia (5% O2 for 10 min), and oral inoculation with commensal fecal flora twice daily for 3 days. Pups were monitored for gut histology scores, mesenteric bacterial translocation, and systemic bacteremia.
Results: Pups from probiotic-fed dams exhibited an 80% decrease in macroscopic gut necrosis, intact mucosal tight junctions, and a significant drop in blood bacteremia compared to controls.
Conclusion: Probiotic interventions confer profound protection against experimental neonatal sepsis and NEC.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mammalian neonatal rat pups, approved Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) / neonatal sepsis model, tested probiotic intervention, published in 2021.
learning_pearl: Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) and neonatal sepsis in mammalian pups are explicitly eligible in our protocol!

title: Effects of carbon monoxide releasing molecule-2 (CORM-2) on intestinal dysmotility in murine cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Tan, S., Wang, X., He, J.
abstract:
Aim: To examine whether CORM-2 improves gastrointestinal motility and reduces systemic cytokine release in septic mice.
Methods: Male ICR mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). CORM-2 (8 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally 1 hour after CLP. Gastrointestinal transit was evaluated at 24 hours using rhodamine-dextran.
Results: CLP induced severe delayed gastric emptying, which was partially restored by CORM-2 treatment alongside decreased serum IL-6.
Conclusion: CORM-2 ameliorates gut dysmotility in murine polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Date violation: Published in 2017. Our search protocol is restricted to studies published from 2020 to present.
learning_pearl: Check publication year: 2017 is before our 2020 cutoff, so exclude under EX-PRE2020.

title: Fibrin clot-associated Klebsiella pneumoniae peritoneal sepsis in sheep: Hemodynamic resuscitation with vasopressin versus norepinephrine
authors: Rehberg, S., Ertmer, C., Morelli, A., et al.
abstract:
Background: Large animal models bridge the translational gap between rodent biology and human intensive care medicine. We evaluated arginine vasopressin (AVP) versus norepinephrine (NE) in ovine live-pathogen peritoneal sepsis.
Methods: Adult female sheep were instrumented with pulmonary artery catheters and arterial lines. Peritoneal sepsis was initiated by intraperitoneal implantation of a standardized fibrin clot infected with 5x10^9 CFU live Klebsiella pneumoniae. Animals received titrated vasopressin or norepinephrine infusions upon development of systemic hypotension.
Results: AVP reduced fluid resuscitation requirements, preserved renal papillary blood flow, and mitigated progressive lactic acidosis compared to high-dose NE.
Conclusions: In ovine fibrin clot Klebsiella sepsis, AVP effectively restores vascular tone while limiting excessive catecholamine exposure.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo large mammalian model (sheep), approved fibrin clot implantation model with live Klebsiella causing peritoneal sepsis, evaluates a therapeutic vasopressor intervention, published in 2020.
learning_pearl: Fibrin clot implantation models in large mammals (sheep/pigs) with live pathogens are explicitly eligible!

title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy attenuates sterile smoke inhalation-induced acute lung injury in rats
authors: Yilmaz, S., Akarsu, M., Ergun, H.
abstract:
Objective: Smoke inhalation causes thermal and chemical bronchial injury leading to respiratory failure. We evaluated hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) therapy in a non-infectious smoke injury model.
Methods: Anesthetized Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed to standardized cool pine smoke for 10 minutes without bacterial infection. Rats were treated with 100% O2 at 2.4 ATA for 60 min or sham chamber air. Lung histologic injury and myeloperoxidase were measured at 24 hours.
Results: HBO exposure reduced alveolar wall thickening and decreased lung MPO levels compared to air-treated animals.
Conclusion: HBO alleviates sterile chemical and thermal smoke-induced pulmonary damage.
rationale: Condition violation: Sterile smoke inhalation injury is a chemical/thermal burn model without sepsis or infectious challenge.
learning_pearl: Sterile lung injury without infection or systemic sepsis is EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Targeting gut microbiota with fecal microbiota transplantation attenuates sepsis-induced acute kidney injury in mice
authors: Sun, J., Ding, X., Wang, Q., et al.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
abstract:
Background: Gut dysbiosis accelerates distant organ failure during polymicrobial sepsis. We tested whether fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy donors protects against sepsis-induced acute kidney injury (SA-AKI).
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Six hours post-CLP, mice were orally administered fecal slurry from healthy wild-type mice or sterile vehicle. Serum creatinine, renal KIM-1, tubular apoptosis (TUNEL), and fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were evaluated at 24 hours.
Results: FMT restored gut microbial diversity, boosted acetate and butyrate levels, reduced serum creatinine (38.2 vs 79.5 μmol/L, p < 0.001), and blunted renal tubular apoptotic death.
Conclusion: FMT confers therapeutic protection against septic acute kidney injury by replenishing beneficial microbial metabolites.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CLP model, therapeutic intervention (fecal microbiota transplant) given after CLP, evaluates renal outcomes, published in 2022.
learning_pearl: Fecal microbiota transplantation is an intervention tested for sepsis. Fully eligible!

title: Abstract 412: Evaluation of synthetic antimicrobial peptide AP-57 in porcine fecal polymicrobial peritonitis
authors: Vance, J. R., Thorne, L. B., Miller, A. C.
abstract:
Introduction: Sepsis remains a leading cause of intensive care mortality. We evaluated the novel synthetic peptide AP-57 in porcine peritonitis.
Methods: Yorkshire pigs underwent fecal slurry peritonitis. Six hours after induction, swine received AP-57 (10 mg/kg IV) or vehicle saline. Hemodynamics and 48-hour survival were monitored.
Results: AP-57 significantly improved mean arterial pressure and boosted survival from 30% to 75% (p < 0.05).
Conclusions: AP-57 demonstrates promising therapeutic efficacy. [Published as a conference abstract only; Society of Critical Care Medicine 51st Critical Care Congress; full text peer-reviewed paper not available].
rationale: Publication type violation: This is a conference abstract without a peer-reviewed full-text primary research article. Our protocol strictly excludes conference abstracts, commentaries, and reviews under EX-NONPRIMARY.
learning_pearl: Watch for conference abstracts in your search results: even if the animal model and drug look great, conference abstracts without a full-text paper must be excluded under EX-NONPRIMARY!

title: Therapeutic administration of anti-interleukin-6 receptor monoclonal antibody in a swine model of Escherichia coli bacteremia
authors: Olsen, T. B., Thomsen, P., Lindhardt, B., et al.
abstract:
Background: Excessive IL-6 signaling precipitates refractory septic shock. We evaluated whether targeted IL-6 receptor blockade improves hemodynamics during Gram-negative bacteremia in swine.
Methods: Anesthetized domestic pigs received an intravenous infusion of live Escherichia coli (10^8 CFU/kg/h) to induce severe bacteremic sepsis. Two hours after onset of bacteremia, animals were randomized to receive anti-IL-6R mAb (5 mg/kg IV) or vehicle control alongside lung-protective ventilation and fluid resuscitation for 24 hours.
Results: Swine receiving anti-IL-6R mAb required 40% less vasopressor support to maintain mean arterial pressure ≥65 mmHg, had lower serum troponin I, and demonstrated preserved systemic vascular resistance.
Conclusions: IL-6 receptor antagonism stabilizes hemodynamics in live-pathogen Gram-negative sepsis in large mammals.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo swine, live E. coli bacteremia sepsis model, therapeutic intervention (anti-IL-6R mAb) given post-infection, published in 2023.
learning_pearl: Live E. coli bacteremic sepsis in swine + therapeutic mAb = perfect match!

title: Ex vivo normothermic machine perfusion with hydrogen gas prevents ischemia-reperfusion injury in isolated rat lungs
authors: Tani, M., Nakano, H., Saito, K.
abstract:
Objective: Donor organ quality limits lung transplantation success. We evaluated hydrogen-rich gas during ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP).
Methods: Lungs were harvested from donor Sprague-Dawley rats and maintained in an ex vivo organ perfusion chamber for 4 hours. Perfused lungs were ventilated with 2% H2 gas or control medical air. Perfusate cytokines and vascular resistance were measured.
Results: H2 gas reduced perfusate IL-1β and prevented vascular resistance elevation in the isolated organ.
Conclusion: Ex vivo hydrogen administration preserves isolated donor lungs during machine perfusion.
rationale: Model violation: Ex vivo isolated organ perfusion circuit without live animal organism.
learning_pearl: Ex vivo isolated organ perfusion models are excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Cecal ligation and puncture variants: Comparing high-grade versus low-grade ligation in female Wistar rats treated with ulinastatin
authors: Fischer, S., Weber, C., Klein, M., et al.
abstract:
Background: Ulinastatin is a broad urinary trypsin inhibitor. We tested its therapeutic efficacy across varying severity grades of cecal ligation and puncture.
Methods: Female Wistar rats underwent either cecal ligation and puncture (CLP, 50% cecal length ligation) or cecal ligation and incision (CLI variant). Animals received ulinastatin (50,000 U/kg IP) or saline at 2 hours and 12 hours post-surgery. Twenty-four-hour organ histology, blood lactate, and 7-day survival were recorded.
Results: Ulinastatin treatment significantly enhanced survival in both CLP (70% vs 35%, p = 0.01) and CLI (55% vs 18%, p = 0.006) cohorts while decreasing hepatic necrosis and serum creatinine.
Conclusion: Ulinastatin provides robust organ-protective and survival benefits across diverse surgical variants of polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved CLP and CLI (cecal ligation and incision) variants, evaluates therapeutic intervention (ulinastatin), 2021 publication.
learning_pearl: CLP variants such as cecal ligation and incision (CLI) are explicitly included!

title: Pathophysiological features of septic shock: A narrative review of animal models and hemodynamic monitoring
authors: De Backer, D., Cecconi, M., Vincent, J. L.
abstract: Review Summary: Preclinical models of sepsis are indispensable tools for elucidating complex microcirculatory derangements. In this review, we examine the relative advantages and limitations of CLP, LPS, and live bacterial infusion models in rodents and large animals. We critically evaluate the clinical relevance of fluid resuscitation protocols and highlight key barriers in translating preclinical discoveries into human intensive care units.
rationale: Design violation: Narrative review article, not primary empirical research.
learning_pearl: Narrative reviews are excluded under EX-NONPRIMARY.

title: Group B Streptococcus neonatal sepsis in newborn piglets: Rescue therapy with a novel synthetic surfactant-peptide formulation
authors: Svensson, K., Lindqvist, E., Holst, M., et al.
abstract:
Background: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for fulminant neonatal sepsis and persistent pulmonary hypertension. We tested a novel peptide-fortified surfactant formulation.
Methods: Newborn piglets (aged 12-24 hours) were inoculated intravenously with live Group B Streptococcus (GBS, 1x10^9 CFU/kg) to trigger acute bacteremic sepsis. Upon onset of hypoxemia, animals received endotracheal instillation of synthetic surfactant enriched with peptide CHF5633 or standard bovine surfactant. Hemodynamics and lung compliance were tracked for 12 hours.
Results: Piglets treated with the peptide formulation maintained higher systemic arterial pressure, exhibited superior gas exchange (PaO2/FiO2 ratio 340 vs 180 mmHg, p < 0.01), and had lower pulmonary vascular resistance.
Conclusion: Peptide-fortified surfactant rescue prevents fatal cardiorespiratory collapse in porcine GBS neonatal sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo piglets, approved Group B Streptococcus (GBS) neonatal sepsis model, evaluates a therapeutic surfactant intervention, published in 2022.
learning_pearl: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) neonatal sepsis is explicitly eligible!

title: Endotoxin-induced uveitis in Sprague-Dawley rats is suppressed by topical dexamethasone eye drops
authors: Chung, Y., Park, J., Kim, S.
abstract:
Purpose: To examine the ocular anti-inflammatory efficacy of dexamethasone in an endotoxin-induced uveitis (EIU) model.
Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats received a subplantar injection of LPS (200 μg) to elicit localized anterior chamber ocular inflammation without systemic septic shock. Dexamethasone eye drops were administered at 2 and 6 hours. Aqueous humor cells and protein were quantified.
Results: Topical dexamethasone reduced infiltrating inflammatory cells in the aqueous humor by 75%.
Conclusion: Topical dexamethasone dampens local endotoxin-induced ocular uveitis.
rationale: Model violation: Pure LPS challenge model (endotoxin-induced uveitis) and does not model systemic sepsis.
learning_pearl: Endotoxin injection models (and local non-sepsis uveitis) are excluded under EX-LPS.

title: Intratracheal inoculation of Klebsiella pneumoniae produces pneumonia-derived sepsis in mice: Therapeutic impact of combined ceftazidime and polymyxin B
authors: Patel, R. N., Joshi, M. D., Shah, A.
abstract:
Background: Pneumonia-derived sepsis accounts for over 50% of clinical sepsis admissions. We evaluated synergistic antibiotic combination therapy against an MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae strain.
Methods: C57BL/6 mice received intratracheal instillation of live K. pneumoniae (10^7 CFU) leading to severe necrotizing lung infection, bacterial dissemination into blood, and systemic septic shock. Mice were treated 6 hours post-inoculation with subcutaneous ceftazidime, polymyxin B, or combination therapy for 5 days. Blood bacterial clearance and survival were evaluated.
Results: Combination therapy achieved complete blood sterilization within 24 hours and increased 10-day survival from 10% in monotherapy to 80% (p < 0.001).
Conclusion: Early combination antimicrobial therapy prevents fatal septicemia in pneumonia-derived sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved pneumonia-derived sepsis model with intratracheal live Klebsiella, therapeutic antibiotic intervention, 2023 publication.
learning_pearl: Pneumonia-derived sepsis with live pathogens (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas) is explicitly included!

title: Galleria mellonella larvae as an in vivo model to assess the antimicrobial activity of novel carvacrol derivatives against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
authors: Lopes, C. F., Martins, P. A., Silva, M.
abstract:
Background: Greater wax moth (Galleria mellonella) larvae are increasingly used as an alternative non-mammalian host for infection studies.
Methods: G. mellonella larvae were injected with 10^5 CFU Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Larvae received hemocoel injections of carvacrol derivatives (5-20 mg/kg) 1 hour post-infection. Melanization scores and larval survival were monitored over 96 hours.
Results: Compound CRV-3 significantly reduced larval melanization and improved survival from 20% to 70% at 72 hours.
Conclusion: G. mellonella provides a robust, ethically favorable screening platform for antibacterial compounds.
rationale: Organism violation: Galleria mellonella (wax moth larvae) are insects (invertebrates), not mammals. Excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.
learning_pearl: Invertebrates (insects, moths, nematodes) are non-mammalian models: EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Combination of vitamin C, hydrocortisone, and thiamine in an experimental rat model of cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Marik, P. E., Bellomo, R., Shaw, A., et al.
abstract:
Background: The 'HAT' protocol (hydrocortisone, ascorbic acid, thiamine) has sparked intense clinical controversy. We tested the triad in a controlled rat CLP model.
Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent CLP. Four hours post-surgery, animals were randomized to receive HAT combination therapy (vitamin C 100 mg/kg, hydrocortisone 5 mg/kg, thiamine 25 mg/kg IV) or vehicle control for 3 days. Arterial blood gas, renal histology, plasma biomarkers, and 96-hour survival were assessed.
Results: Rats treated with the HAT combination demonstrated modest reductions in serum creatinine, but no statistically significant improvement in 96-hour survival was observed (45% vs 40%, p = 0.68).
Conclusion: The HAT combination attenuated biochemical organ injury but failed to improve overall survival in experimental rat polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved CLP model, therapeutic intervention (vitamin C + hydrocortisone + thiamine), vehicle control, published in 2020. Neutral or negative survival results do NOT disqualify a paper!
learning_pearl: Negative or neutral results (no survival improvement) are still INCLUDED as long as a therapeutic intervention was tested!

title: Bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis and respiratory failure in mice: Modulation by pirfenidone
authors: Gao, L., Zhang, J., Zhao, H.
abstract:
Objective: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis causes irreversible architectural distortion. We investigated pirfenidone in a standard bleomycin model.
Methods: C57BL/6 mice received intratracheal bleomycin (2 U/kg) to induce sterile pulmonary fibrosis. Pirfenidone (100 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 21 days. Collagen deposition (Sircol assay) and lung hydroxyproline were measured.
Results: Pirfenidone significantly reduced lung collagen accumulation and inhibited fibrotic myofibroblast differentiation.
Conclusion: Pirfenidone exhibits antifibrotic efficacy in bleomycin-induced fibrotic lung remodeling.
rationale: Condition violation: Bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis is a chronic fibrotic toxicity model, completely unrelated to acute sepsis.
learning_pearl: Sterile lung fibrosis (bleomycin) is not sepsis: EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Administration of mesenchymal stem cell secretome improves survival and dampens cytokine storm in murine fecal pellet peritonitis
authors: Chavez, M. A., Gomez, A., Torres, L., et al.
abstract:
Background: Cell-free therapies utilizing stem cell conditioned medium (secretome) avoid immunological risks of live cell transplantation. We tested MSC secretome in a fecal pellet peritonitis model.
Methods: Male Balb/c mice received an intraperitoneal implantation of a standardized fecal pellet (0.5 mL) to generate polymicrobial peritonitis. Two hours later, mice received tail-vein injections of concentrated MSC secretome or vehicle saline. Peritoneal bacterial load, serum IL-10, TNF-α, and 5-day survival were recorded.
Results: MSC secretome treated mice exhibited enhanced bacterial clearance, elevated systemic IL-10 levels, attenuated lung vascular leak, and improved 5-day survival (58% vs 22%, p = 0.007).
Conclusion: Stem cell secretome acts as a potent therapeutic agent in polymicrobial abdominal sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved fecal pellet implantation sepsis model, therapeutic intervention (MSC secretome), 2021 publication.
learning_pearl: Fecal pellet implantation is specifically listed as an included sepsis model!

title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced acute kidney injury in female rats: Renoprotective effects of N-acetylcysteine
authors: Kucuk, A., Arslan, M., Demirel, C.
abstract:
Context: Septic acute kidney injury is a frequent complication of systemic endotoxemia. We investigated N-acetylcysteine (NAC) in LPS-induced nephrotoxicity.
Materials and Methods: Female Wistar albino rats were injected with Escherichia coli LPS (5 mg/kg IV). NAC (150 mg/kg IP) was administered 30 minutes following LPS challenge. Serum cystatin C, BUN, and renal tissue malondialdehyde were analyzed.
Results: NAC administration reduced oxidative stress biomarkers and improved renal glomerular filtration rates following endotoxin exposure.
Discussion: NAC protects against LPS-induced endotoxemic renal dysfunction.
rationale: Model violation: Pure intravenous LPS injection (endotoxemia model). Excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Pure LPS injection causing acute kidney injury is an endotoxemia model: EX-LPS.

title: Therapeutic hypothermia combined with broad-spectrum antibiotics preserves intestinal microcirculation in porcine polymicrobial peritonitis
authors: Venkatesh, B., Morgan, T., Cohen, J., et al.
abstract:
Objective: Microvascular shut-down in the gut fuels multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. We evaluated mild therapeutic hypothermia (34°C) combined with piperacillin/tazobactam in porcine peritonitis.
Methods: Anesthetized domestic pigs underwent surgical placement of a perforated colon capsule containing autologous feces and live E. coli to elicit abdominal sepsis. At the onset of shock, pigs were cooled to 34°C for 18 hours or maintained normothermic (38°C), both with antibiotics. Sublingual and mesenteric sidestream dark-field imaging tracked perfused vessel density.
Results: Hypothermic pigs demonstrated superior microvascular perfused vessel density (82% vs 54%, p < 0.01), reduced metabolic acidosis, and attenuated mesenteric edema.
Conclusions: Therapeutic hypothermia protects microvascular perfusion during abdominal sepsis in swine.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo swine, approved abdominal polymicrobial peritonitis model, evaluates therapeutic hypothermia + antibiotics, published in 2021.
learning_pearl: Hypothermia and supportive physiological therapies are valid interventions for sepsis!

title: High-throughput proteomic profiling of RAW 264.7 macrophages during inflammatory polarization
authors: Shen, F., Zhou, Y., Huang, L.
abstract: Summary: Macrophage phenotypic switching is critical in inflammation. We analyzed RAW 264.7 macrophage cultures stimulated with heat-killed S. aureus using label-free mass spectrometry. Over 4,200 proteins were identified across 24 hours of stimulation, delineating key metabolic shifts without testing in vivo compounds.
rationale: Model violation: In vitro RAW 264.7 macrophage cell culture only; also no therapeutic candidate tested.
learning_pearl: In vitro proteomics without animal testing is excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Urosepsis induced by transurethral inoculation of uropathogenic Escherichia coli in female Sprague-Dawley rats: Efficacy of cranberry proanthocyanidins
authors: Giacobbe, D. R., Marchese, A., Rossi, R., et al.
abstract:
Background: Urosepsis constitutes up to 25% of human sepsis cases. We evaluated the therapeutic potential of purified cranberry proanthocyanidins (PACs) in an experimental rodent urosepsis model.
Methods: Female Sprague-Dawley rats received transurethral instillation of live uropathogenic E. coli (CFT073, 10^8 CFU) leading to ascending pyelonephritis, bacteremia, and systemic sepsis. Animals were gavaged with PACs (50 mg/kg) or water twice daily starting 12 hours after inoculation. Renal bacterial counts, blood cultures, and serum creatinine were measured.
Results: PAC treatment reduced kidney bacterial burden by 2.4 log10 CFU/g, accelerated blood culture sterilization, and prevented interstitial nephritis-induced renal failure.
Conclusion: Cranberry PACs demonstrate adjunctive therapeutic benefit in experimental Gram-negative urosepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved live-pathogen urosepsis / interstitial nephritis model, evaluates a therapeutic intervention (cranberry PACs), published in 2022.
learning_pearl: Urosepsis and ascending pyelonephritis-induced sepsis are explicitly eligible!

title: A murine model of sterile ischemic stroke: Neuroprotective effects of edaravone
authors: Nakamura, K., Tanaka, M., Ito, Y.
abstract:
Objective: Middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) is the standard model for ischemic stroke. We evaluated edaravone in male mice.
Methods: Transient MCAO (60 min) was induced in C57BL/6 mice via intraluminal filament. Edaravone (3 mg/kg) was injected upon reperfusion. Infarct size and neurological deficit scores were recorded at 24 hours.
Results: Edaravone significantly decreased cerebral infarction volume.
Conclusion: Edaravone reduces ischemic neuronal death.
rationale: Condition violation: Ischemic stroke (MCAO) is an acute focal cerebral ischemia model, not a sepsis model.
learning_pearl: Stroke and ischemic brain injury are not sepsis: EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Delayed administration of recombinant human thrombomodulin attenuates disseminated intravascular coagulation and renal injury in rat CLP sepsis
authors: Watanabe, E., Hirasawa, H., Oda, S., et al.
abstract:
Background: Sepsis-associated coagulopathy drives microvascular thrombosis and organ ischemia. We investigated recombinant human thrombomodulin (rhTM) in rat polymicrobial peritonitis.
Methods: Wistar rats were subjected to CLP. Animals received intravenous rhTM (1 mg/kg) or vehicle saline 4 hours post-CLP. Thrombin-antithrombin complexes (TAT), D-dimer, fibrinogen, renal glomerular microthrombi, and 72-hour survival were assessed.
Results: rhTM treatment blunted plasma TAT elevation, eliminated glomerular fibrin deposition on renal histology, and improved 72-hour survival from 32% to 68% (p = 0.005).
Conclusion: Post-treatment with rhTM prevents microvascular thrombosis and protects renal function in polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved CLP model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (rhTM) administered 4h post-CLP, reports DIC and survival, published in 2020.
learning_pearl: Therapies targeting sepsis-induced coagulopathy/DIC in CLP models are fully eligible!

title: Evaluation of botanical extracts against septic peritonitis in Spanish language cohort
authors: Rodriguez-Morales, A., Gomez, C., Diaz, M.
abstract:
Resumen: Evaluamos el extracto de Calendula officinalis en ratones con ligadura y puncion cecal (CLP). Los ratones recibieron extracto oral (100 mg/kg) post-cirugia. La supervivencia a los 5 dias mostro una mejoria modesta del 40% frente al 25% en controles.
Conclusion: El extracto muestra propiedades antiinflamatorias moderadas en peritonitis.
rationale: Language violation: Published entirely in Spanish. Our protocol specifies that only studies published in English are eligible.
learning_pearl: Only papers published in English are included: non-English papers are excluded under EX-LANG.

title: Therapeutic administration of sodium butyrate restores regulatory T cell balance and enhances bacterial clearance in murine CLP
authors: Farley, K. S., Morris, D. L., Higgins, P. J.
abstract:
Background: Regulatory T cell (Treg) dysregulation contributes to post-septic immune suppression. We evaluated sodium butyrate (NaB) as an epigenetic immunomodulator.
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice underwent medium-grade CLP. Mice received sodium butyrate (100 mg/kg IP) or vehicle saline 3 hours and 24 hours post-CLP. Splenic Treg frequencies, peritoneal fluid bacterial CFU, and 7-day survival were determined.
Results: NaB treatment promoted Treg differentiation, reduced circulating bacterial dissemination by 70%, and boosted 7-day survival from 25% to 60% (p = 0.01).
Conclusions: Sodium butyrate restores adaptive immune homeostasis and reduces lethality in polymicrobial peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CLP model, therapeutic intervention (sodium butyrate) given after surgery, 2023 publication.
learning_pearl: Immunomodulatory interventions given after CLP are valid inclusions!

title: Dexamethasone pre-treatment in lipopolysaccharide-challenged neonatal piglets
authors: Krueger, L. C., Myers, G. R., Bennett, T. H.
abstract:
Objective: Endotoxemia in neonates triggers profound cardiovascular collapse. We investigated dexamethasone pretreatment in young piglets.
Methods: Four-day-old domestic piglets were infused with E. coli LPS (2 μg/kg/h for 4h). Animals received dexamethasone (1 mg/kg IV) or saline 1 hour before LPS initiation. Systemic vascular resistance and pulmonary arterial pressure were continuously tracked.
Results: Dexamethasone reduced pulmonary hypertension but did not prevent cardiac output depression.
Conclusions: Dexamethasone attenuates pulmonary hypertensive spikes during neonatal endotoxemia.
rationale: Model violation: Pure E. coli LPS endotoxin infusion in piglets. Excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Even in piglets, pure LPS infusion is an endotoxin model: EX-LPS.
